body.translated_text: The Characteristics of Images as Spoken by the Perfectly Enlightened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddhabhāṣitaṃ Pratimālakṣaṇam</s>)

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutamekasmin samaye buddho bhagavān jetavane viharati sma / tuṣitavarabhavanāt māturdharmadeśanāgamanakālasamaye śāriputro bhagavantametadavocat / bhagavan bhagavatā gate parinirvṛte vā śrāddhaiḥ kulaputraiḥkuladuhitṛbhiśca kathaṃ pratipattavyam / bhagavānāha - śāriputra! mayi gate parinirvṛte vā nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalaṃ kāyaṃ kartavyam / yāvatkāyaṃ tāvadvyāmaṃ yāvadvyāmaṃ tāvatkāyaṃ pūjāsatkārārthaṃ pratimā kartavyā / sarvāṅgopāṅgāvayavasthaulyalāvaṇyalālityasalīlatvaṃ chatrākāraṃ śiraḥskandhāṃ(dhasu)saṃsthitoṣṇīṣatvādisusaṃsthānāt / tatrāyāmavistāroccheda(tsedha)sandhibandhanirgamaiḥ pramāṇaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sugatānāñca pravakṣyāmi tacchṛṇu / tatra tāvat pramāṇaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ svenāṅgulīpramāṇenaśataṃ viṃśatyuttaram, buddhānāṃ pañcaviṃśatyuttaram /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, was dwelling in the <s>Jetavana</s>. At the time of his return from the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven to teach the <s>Dharma</s> to his mother, <s>Śāriputra</s> spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "<s>Bhagavān</s>, when the <s>Bhagavān</s> has departed or attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, how should faithful sons and daughters of good family act?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "<s>Śāriputra</s>! When I have departed or attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the body should be made with the circumference of a <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree. As long as the body, so long is the arm-span; as long as the arm-span, so long is the body. For the purpose of worship and veneration, images (<s>pratimā</s>) should be made, with beauty, grace, elegance, and charm in all major and minor limbs, with the head in the shape of a parasol (<s>chatrākāra</s>), and with well-formed <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance) established upon the shoulders. Therein, I shall declare the proportions (<s>pramāṇa</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Sugatas</s> in terms of length, width, height, joints, connections, and projections — listen to that. First, the proportion of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is one hundred and twenty by their own finger-measure (<s>aṅguli</s>); for <s>Buddhas</s>, one hundred and twenty-five."

children.translated_text: The <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance) is four <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths), and likewise the area of the hair;
thirteen and a half measures [for the face], and that [face] has three [divisions]. (verse 1)
The forehead, the nose, and below that to the end of the chin — [each being] a third;

children.text: caturaṅgulaṃ lalāṭaṃ ca tulyaṃ nāsikayā bhavet // 2 //
children.translated_text: the forehead is four <s>aṅgulas</s> and should be equal to the nose. (verse 2)

children.text: sādhikaṃ cibukāntaṃ tu cibukaṃ dvayaṅgulaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: The portion to the end of the chin is slightly more; the chin should be two <s>aṅgulas</s>;
its length and projection are considered to be four <s>aṅgulas</s>. (verse 3)
The cheeks are four <s>aṅgulas</s>, extending from the root of the ear;
the jaw should be three <s>aṅgulas</s> in height and two <s>aṅgulas</s> in width. (verse 4)
It should be slightly more, full, like the jaw of a great lion;
the lower lip is two <s>aṅgulas</s> in length, with its projection and height each one measure. (verse 5)

children.text: madhye syācchobhanā rekhā sṛkkaṇī mātṛke smṛtau /
children.translated_text: In the middle there should be a beautiful line; the corners of the mouth are remembered as one measure [each];
the skillful [artist] should make the mouth four <s>aṅgulas</s> in length. (verse 6)
Forty teeth are remembered, positioned as appropriate;
the upper lip should be half an <s>aṅgula</s>, and likewise its height and projection. (verse 7)
The <s>godhī</s> (gum ridge) should be made one-third of an <s>aṅgula</s>, and it remains in position;
the nose is two <s>aṅgulas</s> in width and one and a half <s>aṅgulas</s> in height. (verse 8)

children.text: arddhāṅgule same vṛtte nāsāyāḥ śrotasī smṛtau(te) /
children.translated_text: The nostrils of the nose are remembered as half an <s>aṅgula</s> each, equal and round;
the bridge of the nose is even in the middle, half a measure in width. (verse 9)
The space between the eyes should be known as one <s>aṅgula</s>; the eyes are four <s>aṅgulas</s>;
two <s>aṅgulas</s> in width, in the middle of them the pupil (<s>tārā</s>) is one-third. (verse 10)
The gaze should be five parts [downward]; two <s>aṅgulas</s> and three <s>aṅgulas</s> of those;
one-fourth of an <s>aṅgula</s> extended — the eye is like a casket (<s>samudgaka</s>). (verse 11)
The eye-socket should be made in the shape of a lotus petal, three <s>aṅgulas</s>;
the line from the eyes to the wings of the nose is like an <s>oleander</s> (<s>karavīra</s>) [flower]. (verse 12)

children.text: tārā same ca cibuke sṛkkaṇī pariyojayet /
children.translated_text: The pupils should be aligned with the chin; the corners of the mouth should be connected [in the design];
the space between the eyebrows should be made one and a half <s>aṅgulas</s> wide. (verse 13)
In the middle, the <s>ūrṇā</s> (auspicious mark) should be known — auspicious, resembling the full moon;
the <s>ūrṇā</s> is aligned with the line of the nose-bridge, and likewise the hair rises upward from the crown. (verse 14)
That should be known as the crest-jewel (<s>śiromaṇi</s>), resplendent and stainless;
the crown of the head is four <s>aṅgulas</s> in height above the forehead. (verse 15)
Parasol-shaped, auspicious, dark blue, the hair curls rightward and rises upward;
the eyebrow-line should be four measures; the tip of the ear is the same. (verse 16)
The ears extend two <s>aṅgulas</s>; the ear-lobes are half a measure;
the height should be known as one measure; the ear-holes joined together are half a measure. (verse 17)
One-fourth of an <s>aṅgula</s> is the spiral of the ear in width;
the ear from its inner part should be one and a half measures, [totaling] two <s>aṅgulas</s>. (verse 18)

children.text: pārśvau syātāṃ yathāśobhaṃ keśāścāpi tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: The sides should be [made] according to beauty, and likewise the hair;
the ear-lobe is four and a half measures from the outer corner of the eye. (verse 19)
From ear to ear, the crown of the head should be known as eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s>;
the back [of the head] between them is considered to be fourteen <s>aṅgulas</s>. (verse 20)
The head should be forty measures in circumference.
The neck in height [should be] four <s>mātrā</s>s, and eight <s>mātrā</s>s in width. // 21 //
And in circumference it should be made twenty-four <s>mātrā</s>s.
From the end of the neck, eight <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths); the shoulder is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>. // 22 //
Without a visible inner shoulder-joint, the shoulder should be round and endowed with [auspicious] marks.
The arm in length is desired to be forty <s>mātrā</s>s. // 23 //
The upper arm (<s>bāhu</s>) is twenty <s>mātrā</s>s; the forearm (<s>prabāhu</s>) is likewise sixteen.
The hand-tip is declared [to be] twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> from the wrist (<s>maṇibandha</s>). // 24 //
From the elbow (<s>kukuṇī</s>) and wrist, one <s>aṅgula</s> each is the [standard finger-width] measure, it is said.
The middle circumference of the arm is desired to be twenty <s>mātrā</s>s. // 25 //
The forearm should be sixteen [<s>mātrā</s>s in circumference]; at the wrist, twelve.
The hand in length is seven [<s>aṅgulas</s>]; the palm's width is five. // 26 //
On the palm should be placed [marks of] a conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>), disc (<s>cakra</s>), lotus (<s>padma</s>), thunderbolt (<s>kuliśa</s>), and goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>).
Lines bearing all kinds of auspicious marks should be made, of various types. // 27 //
The middle finger is five <s>aṅgulas</s> long; the index finger (<s>pradeśinī</s>) is shorter by half a joint (<s>parva</s>).
The ring finger (<s>anāmikā</s>) should be made shorter by half an <s>aṅgula</s>. // 28 //
The little finger (<s>kanīyasī</s>) should be made shorter than the ring finger by one joint.
All fingers have three joints; the auspicious nails are half a joint [long]. // 29 //
Above the wrist, the thumb (<s>aṅguṣṭha</s>) is four <s>aṅgulas</s> [long].
Its circumference is the same [four <s>aṅgulas</s>]; and its nail is half a joint. // 30 //
The distance between the thumb and index finger is remembered as three <s>aṅgulas</s>.
The little finger from the wrist should be five <s>aṅgulas</s> in length. // 31 //
The circumference of the hand-tip should be known as twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>.
The girth of one's own fingers should be one-third of their length. // 32 //
Between the neck and the heart, twelve and a half <s>mātrā</s>s.
And between the heart and navel, four [<s>mātrā</s>s]; and the distance between the breasts also [four]. // 33 //
Above the breasts, the armpits (<s>kakṣa</s>) should be made six <s>aṅgulas</s> [wide].
And above that up to the shoulder, nine <s>mātrā</s>s are declared. // 34 //
The width of the chest (<s>uras</s>) is also twenty-five <s>mātrā</s>s.
The chest in circumference should be made three times the width — auspicious. // 35 //
The distance between the breast and the navel is desired as sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s>.
Without piercing, with [only] a joint-hollow [indicated], the navel circle [should be] one <s>aṅgula</s>. // 36 //
From the center of the navel, the circumference is forty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>.
And the waist (<s>kaṭi</s>) in width should be eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s>. // 37 //
The distance between the navel and the private part should be twelve and a half <s>mātrā</s>s.
The private part should be half of that [in length]; from the <s>apāna</s> (lower) region in circumference. // 38 //
The testicles (<s>vṛṣaṇa</s>) are five <s>mātrā</s>s in length, pendulous, four <s>aṅgulas</s> [in width].
Five <s>mātrā</s>s and four — in width and length of the two. // 39 //
The two thighs (<s>ūru</s>) should be made well-proportioned, twenty-five <s>mātrā</s>s [long].
The space between them should be measured as twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>, well-proportioned. // 40 //
In circumference also, it should be made an auspicious thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>.
In the middle ......... four <s>aṅgulas</s> from the knee. // 41 //

body.translated_text: The joint-binding (<s>sandhibandha</s>) is four <s>mātrā</s>s; the knee and ankle [are respectively] three and two.
[With] concealed ankles, [well-placed] veins, the two [legs should be] delicate [and] auspicious. // 42 //

children.translated_text: The shanks (<s>jaṅghā</s>) should be straight, round, and elongated, twenty-five <s>mātrā</s>s [long].
In their middle, the circumference is twenty-one <s>mātrā</s>s. // 43 //
[The lower shank extends] fourteen <s>aṅgulas</s> in length; from the ankle downward, four <s>aṅgulas</s>.
The ankle is twelve [<s>aṅgulas</s>] in circumference; the foot is half the foot-length in width. // 44 //
The sides are two <s>aṅgulas</s> in width; and the heel (<s>pārṣṇi</s>) is four <s>aṅgulas</s>.
Six <s>aṅgulas</s> in width, [and] three times that in circumference. // 45 //
The five toes have two joints [each]; the nails are remembered as half a joint [long].
Five <s>aṅgulas</s> in circumference; the big toe (<s>aṅguṣṭha</s>) is three <s>aṅgulas</s> long. // 46 //
The second toe (<s>pradeśinī</s>) is equal to the big toe in length.
The remaining [toes] are successively shorter by one-sixteenth, one-eighth, [and] one-eighth. // 47 //
The toes in height are one <s>mātrā</s>; the big toe is one and a half <s>mātrā</s>s.
There, the nails are copper-colored; the toes [are] soft and elongated. // 48 //
The feet are like the back of a tortoise, full, adorned on the outside,
Evenly joined, not drooping, without gaps, well-established, [endowed] with [auspicious] marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). // 49 //
The soles of the two [feet] should be made with beautiful patterns including the wheel (<s>cakra</s>) and other [marks].
These feet are praised by the omniscient ones (<s>sarvajña</s>), who are free from sin. // 50 //
Egg-shaped (<s>kukkuṭāṇḍa</s>), sesame-shaped (<s>tilākāra</s>), square (<s>caturasra</s>), and well-rounded (<s>suvartula</s>) —
these are the four types of face for all general classes [of beings]. // 51 //
For great men, <s>asuras</s>, and women, [the face should be] egg-shaped or sesame-shaped;
these two face [types] are graceful (<s>lāvaṇya</s>) and beautiful — one should make [them thus]. // 52 //
For <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), <s>piśācas</s> (goblins), and <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), the form is distorted;
circular and square — one should make these two face [types]. // 53 //
The gaze of <s>Buddhas</s> in their looking is even and serene (<s>prasanna</s>),

children.text: nādho nordhvaṃ na dainyena saṃyuktaṃ sarvadarśinām // 54 //
children.translated_text: neither downward nor upward, nor conjoined with wretchedness — [such is the gaze] of the all-seeing ones (<s>sarvadarśin</s>). // 54 //

body.translated_text: // Thus concludes the <s>Pratimālakṣaṇa</s> (Characteristics of Images) spoken by the Perfectly Enlightened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>). //
